9958dcfe79c7dcfa9657bf6710ac6433077bb4fa.summary: Silent Push Threat Team blog (published 2024-10-02) on FIN7, described as a financially motivated group with ties to Russia. FIN7 is said to run at least seven fake 'AI deepnude' generator sites and 'free download' and 'free trial' honeypots that deliver Redline Stealer, D3F@ck Loader and Lumma Stealer. A separate malvertising campaign pushes NetSupport RAT through fake browser-extension pages that lead to .MSIX malware. The report describes SEO tactics and shell websites, and says the sites found were taken offline after takedown requests. Silent Push counts 4,000+ FIN7 domains and IPs.…

996cbdff883d200909484667f098b59aa60e31b0.summary: BleepingComputer, citing Cybereason Nocturnus Team research, reports that APT35, described as an Iranian state-backed group, is deploying a new PowerShell-based backdoor called PowerLess along with info stealers and keyloggers. The researchers found potential connections to Memento ransomware, which the report says has been active since April 2021 and has targeted VMware vCenter servers. The article also cites a November joint advisory from US and UK agencies and Microsoft's tracking of six Iranian threat groups using ransomware.

99413f03171db34e715c6c04b5644af977996e87.summary: Mandiant's M-Trends 2024 special report covers its 2023 incident response investigations. Exploits were the most common initial access route, led by zero-day flaws in MOVEit Transfer (CVE-2023-34362) and Barracuda Email Security Gateway (CVE-2023-2868), which the report links to FIN11 and UNC4841. Median dwell time fell to 10 days, and ransomware rose to 23% of investigations. The report also describes China-nexus attacks on edge devices and hypervisors, and North Korea's APT43.
